issues.description: Basic usage example uses next() over a generator where indexing would be clearer
issues.detail: `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is gratuitously clever for documentation that teaches the API. Use `pipeline.nodes[0]` or an explicit name lookup. Readers learning the API will copy-paste this as a pattern and propagate it.

issues.description: ImagePreview example contains unreachable code after the return statement
issues.detail: The example returns the URL form, then shows a commented-out data URI return below. A skimming reader sees two returns and pauses. Split into two distinct named example functions or branch on a parameter rather than leaving dead-looking returns.

issues.description: CustomPreview example uses `[...]` Ellipsis literals as placeholders that will not run
issues.detail: `"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]` is Python-legal but produces Ellipsis on serialization and misleads readers. Use `[]` with an explanatory comment or include one concrete element. Documentation examples should be copy-paste-correct or visibly incomplete.

issues.description: meta parameter complects value-metadata with renderer configuration
issues.detail: meta is documented as both general metadata (versions, timestamps) and renderer control (Mermaid layout, syntax language). One field carrying two unrelated concerns will trap users. Docs should name the split or recommend separating renderer hints from data metadata rather than normalizing the conflation.

issues.description: Standalone node(...) snippets lack imports, definitions, and Pipeline wrappers
issues.detail: Mermaid-config and code-preview examples present bare `node(...)` calls referencing undefined functions like `process_data` and `calculate_metrics`, without importing `node` or wrapping in `Pipeline([...])`. Either make each snippet self-contained and runnable, or mark it explicitly as a fragment.

issues.description: Closure 'data context' pattern hides snapshot time and dodges the input/output limitation
issues.detail: The make_preview_fn closure captures sample_data at pipeline-construction time but is invoked later, looking live. Docs also bury the admission that preview_fn cannot see node inputs/outputs. Name this as a known limitation and state when the snapshot was taken, rather than presenting the workaround as the recommended pattern.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a documentation patch for an experimental preview_fn feature that is broadly useful but has small, propagating sloppiness in its examples: a gratuitous next()-over-generator, dead-looking return statements, Ellipsis-literal placeholders, and bare node() snippets that reference undefined functions. Beyond surface polish, the docs normalize design complecting — meta carries both value-metadata and renderer config, and the closure 'data context' pattern obscures snapshot timing while burying the input/output access limitation. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK on examples and clearer naming of experimental/load-bearing surfaces before merge.
